key_takeaways: Rational numbers are written as p/q (q != 0) and always produce terminating or recurring decimal expansions.
Between any two rational numbers lie infinitely many other rational (and irrational) numbers.
Irrational numbers cannot be expressed as p/q, and their decimals never terminate or repeat.
Irrational lengths like sqrt(2), sqrt(3), sqrt(n) can be constructed geometrically using right-angled triangles (Baudhāyana-Pythagoras theorem / Square Root Spiral).
Combining rational and irrational numbers fills every gap, creating the continuous Real Number Line (R).
Modern mathematics extends beyond real numbers to Imaginary Numbers (i = sqrt(-1)) to solve square roots of negative values.
